title: Runtime 1.22 release plan for KV cache compaction (readiness, docs, staged rollout approvals)
creator: Talia Benson
body:
## Summary
Coordinate release readiness for runtime-1.22 shipping KV cache compaction + tier-aware eviction behind feature flags, including documentation, rollout approvals, canary gates, and rollback criteria with Release Eng + SRE.

This ticket is the *release coordination umbrella* (not the implementation). The implementation work is tracked in ENG-4822/4823/4824/4825/4826/4827, and perf validation in ENG-4828 + benchmark artifacts.

## Why now
We have repeated burst-driven tail latency spikes (p95/p99) correlated with KV arena fragmentation under mixed-length decode workloads. runtime-1.22 is the planned train to carry the compaction + eviction mitigation with guardrails, metrics, and a kill-switch.

## Owners / stakeholders
- Release train lead: Connor O'Brien (assignee)
- Program tracking: Talia Benson (creator)
- Runtime TL: Omar El-Sayed
- Scheduler integration: Sofia Ivanova
- SRE sign-off: Sean Gallagher
- Observability standards: Allison Grant
- Oncall readiness/runbooks: Rafael Mendes
- Telemetry rollout policy: Paula Mendes

## Release contents (runtime-1.22)
Expected landing set (refer to PRs / final SHAs when cut):
- Fragmentation + allocator health metrics: pr-19342
- Core allocator + relocation primitives behind FF: pr-19357
- Scheduler budgeting integration (avoid decode stalls): pr-19371
- Tier-aware eviction policy + pinned sessions handling: pr-19388
- Compaction tracing spans/exemplars: pr-19405
- Kill-switch + config plumbing + safe-disable semantics: pr-19422
- Cancellation edge-case fix (relocation during cancel): pr-19440
- Release notes/docs linking: pr-19461

## Docs required before expanding rollout
Blocking docs (must be published + linked from release notes):
- Confluence runbook: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/runtime-kv-cache-compaction-runbook.json
- Tail latency guardrails (SRE): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-tail-latency-guardrails.json
- Metrics standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/kv-cache-fragmentation-metrics-standard.json
- Known risks / mitigations: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/kv-cache-compaction-known-risks.json
- Benchmark plan + thresholds: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/kv-fragmentation-benchmark-plan.json
- Release note entry: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/runtime-1-22-kv-cache-compaction.json

Non-blocking (but preferred before Dedicated expansion):
- Profiling playbook additions: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/kv-cache-compaction-profiling.json

## Rollout plan (staged)
All stages must be feature-flagged and reversible. Default flags remain OFF until SRE sign-off.

Stage 0: Internal perf canary + staging
- Enable in perf-canary scenario cohort only (ENG-4828)
- Validate regression thresholds (p50/p95/p99 + throughput) vs baseline
- Confirm metrics dashboards exist and alert routes are correct (ENG-4830)

Stage 1: Hosted API internal canary
- 1% of hosted traffic in 1 region (us-east) on a single pool
- Guardrails: auto-rollback if p99 decode latency breaches threshold OR if compaction bytes-moved/min exceeds cap for >N minutes and correlates with tail spikes
- Run for 24 hours min; extend to 72 hours if weekend/low staffing

Stage 2: Hosted API expanded canary
- 10% traffic in 2 regions (us-east + eu-west)
- Confirm no increase in request shedding / OOM events
- Confirm eviction counters are within expected band and no correctness alarms

Stage 3: Dedicated (opt-in pools)
- Enable for 1–2 dedicated customers with known burst tail pain (coordinate via PM + CSM)
- Keep tighter budgets by default for Dedicated until we have pool-specific tuning

Stage 4: Broader enablement
- Expand to additional hosted pools; consider default-on for select models/profiles once steady

## Rollback / kill-switch
- Primary kill-switch: runtime flag to disable compaction worker + relocation steps (leaves allocator changes in place).
- Secondary control: disable eviction path (if eviction selection has unexpected side effects).
- Authority during incident: SRE oncall may flip kill-switch unilaterally; runtime oncall paged immediately after (per Sean/Rafael email thread).
- Rollback criteria (candidate; final thresholds owned by SRE):
  - p99 latency regression > +8% for 10 min sustained on canary cohort vs control
  - error rate increase (5xx) > +0.2% absolute in canary cohort
  - OOM / forced shedding events increase in canary cohort
  - compaction time per step consistently exceeds budgeted cap OR scheduler shows decode stalls correlated with compaction spans

## Release readiness checklist
### Code / build
- [ ] All PRs merged to release branch with backports as needed
- [ ] CI green on runtime-1.22 branch
- [ ] Perf-canary scenario (mixed-length bursts) running and reporting
- [ ] Verify feature flag defaults in each environment (dev/staging/prod)
- [ ] Verify config propagation latency meets “safe disable” expectations (platform thread 1768080411)

### Observability
- [ ] Dashboard panels exist (fragmentation ratio, bytes moved, compaction time, eviction rate, p99 correlation)
- [ ] Alerts configured + routed to eng-sre + runtime oncall
- [ ] Traces include compaction/eviction spans and exemplars

### Correctness / safety
- [ ] Stress tests (ENG-4827) passing: cancellations, long-lived sessions, adversarial churn
- [ ] Eviction policy: pinned sessions + prefix caching interactions validated

### Docs / comms
- [ ] Runbook published + linked from release notes
- [ ] SRE guardrails doc published
- [ ] Release note entry published
- [ ] Comms to #eng-releases + #eng-oncall with kill-switch location and rollback criteria

## Cross-links
- Epic: ENG-4821
- PM guardrails/rollback policy: PM-612
- Support context: SUP-28411 / SUP-28433 / SUP-28472
- Relevant Slack threads: #eng-releases (1767911442), #eng-sre (1767652300, 1768072218), #eng-oncall (1767660044), incident thread (1767735109)

## Open questions
1) Final default budgets by tier (Hosted vs Dedicated) and model profile (need sign-off from Omar + Sean).
2) Automated rollback trigger should use absolute p99 vs control-delta vs SLO breach (Paula/Sean to confirm).
3) Whether to enable eviction concurrently with compaction in early canary, or stage them separately.

## Execution notes
This ticket should remain the single place we track:
- release cut date and go/no-go
- sign-offs (Runtime TL, SRE, Release Eng)
- links to the final release note and runbook
- the canary cohort plan and any threshold changes made during rollout
comments: 2026-01-10 (Connor O'Brien): Created runtime-1.22 release checklist in this ticket. Will not cut branch until kill-switch plumbing (ENG-4826) is in and SRE confirms ownership of rollback knobs.

2026-01-18 (Sean Gallagher): +1 on explicit authority: SRE oncall can flip compaction kill-switch without waiting for runtime, but runtime must be paged immediately. Please put this in runbook + #eng-oncall announcement. Also need metric names to match the standard doc before we wire alerts.

2026-01-23 (Allison Grant): Metrics naming: please ensure fragmentation ratio is emitted as both gauge and distribution by model/pool. Eviction counters must be labeled by tier and reason. I’ll review ENG-4830 once dashboard panels are drafted.

2026-01-29 (Omar El-Sayed): Prefer staged enablement: enable compaction first, eviction second. Eviction can mask allocator issues and complicate root cause in early canary. Scheduler budgeting is non-negotiable for prod canary.

2026-02-06 (Rafael Mendes): Oncall runbook needs: (1) how to verify FF state per pool, (2) what dashboards to check first, (3) immediate rollback steps, (4) escalation path. I can help draft but need final flag names and config keys.

2026-02-12 (Connor O'Brien): Targeting branch cut mid-week of 2026-02-17. Waiting on perf-canary mixed-length scenario to be green for 48h and on the cancellation edge-case fix to be merged/backported.

2026-02-14 (Paula Mendes): For automated rollback, we can implement a control-vs-canary delta check on p99 decode + a hard ceiling check vs SLO. Need the final thresholds; suggest start conservative for 1% canary and relax after 72h clean.
2026-02-19 (Connor O'Brien): Update: pr-19440 merged; backport queued. Docs PR (pr-19461) in review. Once runbook + guardrails are published, we can schedule the 1% hosted canary with SRE coverage.

2026-02-21 (Sean Gallagher): SRE sign-off pending dashboard verification (ENG-4830) and confirmation that disabling compaction fully stops page moves (no partial relocation) within one config propagation interval. Please add a note in runbook about expected drain time after flipping kill-switch.
